title: Count the Number of Houses at a Certain Distance I
summary: Given positive integers n, x, and y, find the number of house pairs for each distance k (1 to n) where k is the minimum streets needed to travel between any two houses.
statement: Given positive integers n, x, and y, find the number of house pairs for each distance k (1 to n) where k is the minimum streets needed to travel between any two houses. Return a 1-indexed array where each element represents the count of such pairs for the corresponding distance.
constraints: Houses one through n form a path, plus one extra undirected street between x and y; x may equal y.
Count ordered pairs of distinct houses by their shortest-path distance.
Return n counts where index d-1 stores the number of ordered pairs at distance d.
hints: Any shortest route either stays on the path or uses the extra street in one of two directions.
Enumerate unordered endpoint pairs, take the minimum of those three route lengths, and add both orientations.
For i<j compute min(j-i,|i-x|+1+|j-y|,|i-y|+1+|j-x|); add two to its bucket.
A shortest path never benefits from traversing the one extra edge more than once, so the three cases exhaust all routes.
editorial: A shortest path never benefits from traversing the one extra edge more than once, so the three cases exhaust all routes.

tests.explanation: All six ordered pairs are one street apart after adding the endpoint shortcut.
The counts by distances one, two, and three are ten, eight, and two; larger distances have zero pairs.
